what: Component-wise decomposition of the CARRADA-informed background intervention.

arms.arm: original (1 look, no profile, no ridge)

findings.multilook_is_clean: Multi-look averaging moves the background spread from ~5.57 dB to ~1.59 dB and leaves BOTH lag-1 correlations unchanged, as the theory requires: averaging independent looks divides the variance by L and preserves the correlation coefficient.
findings.profile_causes_the_regression: The range profile is the sole cause of the lag-1 increase, in both axes. It is also what lifts the frame-level dB spread from the within-block value to CARRADA's frame-level value, so the same component is responsible for a match and for a regression.
findings.profile_inflation_is_real: CARRADA shows the same inflation: its within-block lag-1 range is 0.459 against 0.557 at frame level, and its within-block lag-1 Doppler is 0.025 against 0.228. The profile's common-mode effect is a property of the real domain, not an artefact of the generator.
findings.the_residual_is_the_baseline: What the intervention cannot fix is the BASELINE speckle correlation, which the frozen Blackman windows set at 0.57 in both axes against CARRADA's 0.459 (range) and 0.025 (Doppler). Adding a correct profile on top of a baseline that is already too high overshoots.
findings.ridge_is_orthogonal: The ridge changes no background statistic, because the zero-Doppler band is excluded from the background population by the shared protocol.
